Count lines with scope in the component; the count must equal the number of th lines.
Run axe with the th-has-data-cells rule on the users page.

K-022318.example: A thead th with scope='col' reading Name is announced as the label for each cell below it. A tbody th with scope='row' reading Ada Lovelace is announced as the label for each cell in its row.
K-022318.check: rg prints the same number as the th line count, and npx axe prints 0 violations.
traps: Using td for headers removes the header role entirely.
Adding scope to td cells is invalid HTML.
Giving scope='col' to a row header means its row label is never announced.

steps.do: Open the table component and locate the div with class overflow-x-auto.
Add tabindex='0', role='region', and aria-label='Users table, scrollable' to that div.
Add focus-visible:ring-2 and focus-visible:ring-blue-700 to the same div so focus shows a ring.
Write a Playwright test that tabs to the wrapper and presses ArrowRight, then checks that scrollLeft increases.
Run the keyboard scroll test file.

K-022319.example: <div class='overflow-x-auto' tabindex='0' role='region' aria-label='Users table, scrollable'> lets keyboard users focus the scroll area and move it with arrow keys. The blue-700 ring measures about 6.7:1 against white, above the 3:1 minimum for focus indicators.
K-022319.check: Playwright prints 1 passed, and the test confirms scrollLeft is greater than 0 after ArrowRight.
traps: Adding tabindex to the table element does not make the scroll container focusable.
Using role='region' without aria-label leaves the region unnamed.
Using outline-none with no replacement ring removes the focus indicator.

steps.do: Open the table component and find each button inside a th.
Give each button the classes min-h-11, min-w-11, inline-flex, and items-center so its hit area is 2.75rem, which is 44px at a 16px root size.
Add focus-visible:ring-2, focus-visible:ring-offset-2, and focus-visible:ring-blue-700 to each button.
Create the reports folder for Lighthouse output.
Run Lighthouse on the users page with only the accessibility category and save JSON to reports/users.json.
Read the accessibility score from the saved report.

K-022320.example: A button with min-h-11 min-w-11 inline-flex items-center has a 44px by 44px hit area. Lighthouse then reports an accessibility score of 1 when no target-size or focus failures remain.
K-022320.check: jq prints 1, and the Lighthouse report lists no failing target-size audit.
traps: Setting only h-6 leaves the hit area below 44px.
Removing the focus ring with outline-none drops the visible focus indicator.
A Lighthouse score does not prove keyboard focus works, so a Playwright test is still needed.

steps.do: Open the table component and find the sortable th elements.
Set aria-sort to ascending, descending, or none on each th based on the current sort state.
Put a button inside each sortable th so keyboard users can activate sorting.
Write a Playwright test that clicks the Name header button and checks the th aria-sort attribute.
Run the sort test file.
Count aria-sort attributes in the component; the count must equal the number of sortable th elements.

K-022321.example: After one click on Name, the th reads aria-sort='ascending' and the other sortable headers keep aria-sort='none'. The Playwright test asserts toHaveAttribute with aria-sort set to ascending.
K-022321.check: Playwright prints 1 passed, and rg prints the number of sortable th elements.
traps: Putting aria-sort on the button instead of the th misses the column state.
Setting aria-sort on a non-sortable column misleads users.
Forgetting to flip the value on the second click leaves the state wrong.

steps.do: Open the table component and list the text and background classes used on td cells.
Use odd:bg-white and even:bg-gray-50 for stripes and text-gray-900 for cell text, which measures about 17:1.
Search the component for gray text classes so light grays on white rows are found.
Run axe with only the color-contrast rule on the users page.
Count text-gray-400 uses in the component; the count must be 0 because gray-400 on white measures about 2.5:1.

K-022322.example: text-gray-900 (#111827) on bg-gray-50 (#f9fafb) measures about 17:1, well above the 4.5:1 minimum for normal text. A row using text-gray-400 (#9ca3af) on bg-white measures about 2.5:1 and must be replaced with text-gray-700 or darker.
K-022322.check: npx axe prints 0 color-contrast violations and exits with code 0, and rg prints 0 for text-gray-400.
traps: Using text-gray-300 on white rows fails AA.
Checking only one stripe color misses the even rows.
Judging contrast by eye instead of measuring 4.5:1 lets low-contrast text pass.

steps.do: Create the styles directory for the token file.
Add --text-sm at 0.875rem, --text-base at 1rem and --text-lg at 1.125rem inside the :root block of src/styles/tokens.css.
Add --leading-tight at 1.25 and --leading-normal at 1.5 in the same :root block.
Confirm the app entry file imports the token file once.
Confirm the Card styles use only var(--text-) tokens and no raw px font sizes.

K-022323.example: The Card title uses font-size: var(--text-lg) and line-height: var(--leading-tight) from tokens.css. A grep for font-size in src/components/Card returns only lines containing var(--text-, with no px values.
K-022323.check: The grep for tokens.css in src/main.tsx prints one import line, and the rg command prints only font-size lines that contain var(--text-.
traps: A small model often hardcodes 18px in Card.module.css instead of referencing the token. Always use var(--text-lg).
Tokens must be declared on :root or they will not resolve in child components. Check the :root block first.

steps.do: Create src/tokens/typography.ts with a const object that maps names like sizeLg to the CSS variable strings.
Mark the object with as const so that the key names become literal types.
Import the map in src/components/Card/Card.tsx using a named import from the token file.
Run the TypeScript compiler without emitting files to prove the types resolve.

K-022324.example: The file exports typography with sizeLg set to var(--text-lg) and leadingTight set to var(--leading-tight). Card.tsx applies them through the style prop, so a typo like typography.sizeLG fails the build.
K-022324.check: npx tsc --noEmit exits with code 0 and prints no errors.
traps: A small model may forget as const, which widens strings to type string and removes autocomplete. Add as const to the object.
Do not put raw pixel numbers in the map when the CSS variable is the source of truth. Keep the map to var() strings.

steps.do: Render the title in the Card component as an h3 element with a className from the CSS module.
Set font-size to var(--text-lg), font-weight to 600 and line-height to var(--leading-tight) on the .title class in Card.module.css.
Create the browser test file that reads the computed style of the title.
Run the Playwright test that checks the computed font size of the title.

K-022325.example: The title h3 has computed font-size 18px and line-height 22.5px at a 1.125rem base with a 16px root size. The test asserts that getComputedStyle returns 18px.
K-022325.check: npx playwright test prints 1 passed and the computed font size is 18px.
traps: A small model often uses a div for the title, which breaks the heading order. Use h3 for a card title inside a section with an h2.
Computed size depends on the root font size. Assert 18px only when the root is 16px.

steps.do: Add --space-4 with the value 1rem in the :root block of src/styles/tokens.css.
Set padding on the .card class in Card.module.css to var(--space-4) with no other numeric padding.
Search the Card styles for every padding declaration to confirm each one uses a token.
Run the Playwright test that measures the computed padding of the card root.

K-022326.example: A card at a 16px root size has computed padding of 16px on all four sides. The search for padding returns only lines containing var(--space-.
K-022326.check: The rg command prints only lines with var(--space-, and the Playwright test prints 1 passed with padding 16px.
traps: A small model may write padding 16px, which skips the token and breaks theming. Always write the var() form.
Shorthand padding with two values can hide a raw number. Read every line the search prints.

steps.do: Define --color-text-primary and --color-surface in the :root block of src/styles/tokens.css with values that give a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1.
Apply color var(--color-text-primary) and background-color var(--color-surface) to the .body class in Card.module.css.
Start the local dev server in the background so the accessibility scanner can reach the page.
Run the axe accessibility scanner against the page that renders the Card and check for color-contrast violations.

K-022327.example: Text #1a1a1a on a #ffffff surface gives a contrast ratio of 16.7:1, above the 4.5:1 minimum. The axe scan reports zero color-contrast violations for the Card.
K-022327.check: npx axe prints 0 violations for the rule color-contrast.
traps: A small model may pick a light gray text color that fails 4.5:1 on white. Compute the ratio before accepting a color.
Axe only checks rendered states. Test the hover and focus colors separately if they change the text color.

steps.do: Add a selector for html with data-theme set to dark in src/styles/tokens.css and redefine --color-text-primary and --color-surface there.
Make sure no Card style sets a raw hex color, so every color comes from a token.
Run the Playwright test that toggles data-theme and reads the computed text color of the Card.

K-022328.example: Setting data-theme to dark on the html element changes the Card text color from #1a1a1a to #f0f0f0 with no edits to Card.module.css. The theme test asserts the new computed color for both themes.
K-022328.check: The rg command prints no output and the Playwright test prints 2 passed.
traps: A small model may add a second copy of the card styles for dark mode. Override only the tokens, not the component rules.
Dark theme tokens must still meet 4.5:1 contrast. Run the axe scan again after switching the theme.

steps.do: Create the folder for the onboarding css.
Create the plan file that lists the breakpoints.
Write exactly three breakpoints in PLAN.md: 360px phone, 768px tablet, and 1024px desktop, one per line, each with its layout change.
Count the lines that contain px to confirm the plan has three breakpoints.

K-022329.example: PLAN.md contains the line '360px: single column with stacked steps' followed by '768px: two columns with progress bar beside the form' and '1024px: three columns with side illustration.' The grep command prints 3.
traps: Small models copy breakpoints from a framework default like Bootstrap instead of the target device widths.
A plan with no count step cannot be verified.
Keep the plan to three or four breakpoints for a short onboarding flow.

steps.do: In onboarding.css, write the base styles first with display: grid and grid-template-columns: 1fr for the step container.
Add one media query with min-width: 48rem that sets grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr for the step container.
List the media query lines to confirm there is one block with min-width: 48rem.
Check that the stylesheet follows the formatting rules.

K-022330.example: The base rule sets .steps to display: grid with grid-template-columns: 1fr, and the 48rem block changes it to 1fr 1fr. The rg command prints one line that contains min-width: 48rem.
K-022330.check: rg -n @media prints one line containing min-width: 48rem, and npx prettier --check exits with code 0.
traps: Small models write desktop styles first and then undo them for phones.
Using a pixel breakpoint like 768px instead of 48rem ignores the user's text size setting.
Adding a second media query for the same width splits the rules with no benefit.

steps.do: In onboarding.css, give every button and link a min-height of 44px and a min-width of 44px.
Set the heading font size with clamp, using a minimum of 1.5rem, a fluid middle value of 5vw, and a maximum of 2.25rem.
Confirm that the 44px minimum height appears in the stylesheet.
Confirm that the stylesheet uses clamp for the heading size.

K-022331.example: The rule button.primary sets min-height: 44px and min-width: 44px. The heading rule sets font-size: clamp(1.5rem, 5vw, 2.25rem).
K-022331.check: rg -n 'min-height: 44px' prints at least one line, and rg -n clamp prints at least one line that contains clamp(1.5rem, 5vw, 2.25rem).
traps: Small models set touch targets of 24px because that fits a dense layout.
Setting font sizes in px prevents users from scaling text.
Applying min-height to a span instead of a button gives no tap area.

steps.do: Start a local server for the onboarding folder in a second terminal and leave it running.
Write a Playwright test that loads the page at 360px and at 1280px and checks document.documentElement.scrollWidth is less than or equal to clientWidth at each size.
Run the Playwright test file.

K-022332.example: The test sets the viewport to width 360 and height 740, loads http://localhost:8000/, and runs the scrollWidth check. The run reports 2 passed for the two viewport widths.
K-022332.check: npx playwright test prints 2 passed and exits with code 0.
traps: Small models test only at desktop width and skip the phone check.
A fixed pixel width element like a 500px card causes overflow even when the page looks fine.
Playwright tests need the server running first, or they fail with connection refused.

steps.do: Start the local server for the onboarding folder in a second terminal if it is not already running.
Run Lighthouse on the page and limit it to the accessibility category, writing the report to a JSON file.
Read the accessibility score from the report.

K-022333.example: The Lighthouse run writes onboarding/a11y.json, and the jq command prints 0.96 for a page with labeled buttons and alt text on images. Any score below 0.90 means the page needs fixes before handoff.
K-022333.check: jq .categories.accessibility.score onboarding/a11y.json prints a number of 0.90 or higher.
traps: Small models read the score as a percentage and report 96 when the value is 0.96.
A Lighthouse run against a server that is not running writes an error report with no score.
A high Lighthouse score does not prove the touch targets are 44px, so check those separately.

steps.do: Confirm darkMode is set to class in the Tailwind config file.
Rebuild the Tailwind CSS from the input file into dist.
Count compiled dark background rules; zero means the class was never generated.

K-022334.example: The config line prints darkMode: 'class', and the count prints 1 for dark:bg-blue-500 in the button source. If the count prints 0, the file glob in the Tailwind content setting does not cover the button component.
K-022334.check: The grep for darkMode prints one line with darkMode: 'class', and the compiled count is 1 or more.
traps: Tailwind v4 uses an @custom-variant dark rule instead of a darkMode config key, so a missing darkMode line is not always an error.
If the content glob skips the component folder, dark: classes are never generated and the count is 0.
A count of 1 proves the rule exists, not that the page adds the dark class.

steps.do: Confirm the contrast spec file exists before running it.
Run the spec that reads computed text and background colors for light and dark button states.
Confirm the spec asserts a minimum ratio of 4.5 for normal text.

K-022335.example: White text on bg-blue-600 (#2563eb) is about 5.2:1 and passes. White text on bg-blue-400 (#60a5fa) is about 2.5:1 and fails the 4.5:1 minimum.
K-022335.check: The Playwright output ends with N passed and 0 failed, and the grep prints a line containing 4.5.
traps: Light-mode passing does not prove dark-mode passing, so the spec must check both themes.
Hover and disabled states change the colors, so test those states too.
Opacity utilities like disabled:opacity-50 lower the contrast of the label.

steps.do: Confirm the dev server answers on the dark route with HTTP 200.
Run axe on the dark route with WCAG 2 AA rules and exit nonzero on violations.
Run axe on the light route the same way to compare.

K-022336.example: The dark route prints 0 violations for a button using text-white on dark:bg-blue-500 with a 5.2:1 ratio. A dark-mode label set to text-gray-500 on bg-gray-900 fails and axe lists it as a color-contrast violation.
K-022336.check: Both axe runs print 0 violations and exit with code 0, and curl prints HTTP/1.1 200 OK.
traps: axe only checks the state that is rendered when it runs, so hover and focus states need their own test.
The route must actually apply the dark class, otherwise the dark scan repeats the light scan.
A passing scan does not measure ring or border contrast for non-text elements.

steps.do: Confirm the Button component sets a dark focus-visible ring class.
Run the spec that measures the focus ring color against the dark background.
Confirm the spec asserts a non-text contrast minimum of 3.

K-022337.example: ring-blue-400 (#60a5fa) on gray-900 (#111827) is about 7.0:1 and passes 3:1. ring-gray-800 (#1f2937) on gray-900 is about 1.2:1 and fails.
K-022337.check: The grep prints a line with toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(3), and Playwright prints N passed with 0 failed.
traps: The 3:1 minimum is for non-text indicators, not the 4.5:1 text minimum.
Ring color must be compared to the background behind the button, not the page color alone.
A ring that is dark on a dark background can disappear even if the class name is present.

steps.do: Confirm the Button component sets min-h-11 for a 44px minimum height.
Run the spec that reads the button bounding box height in light and dark themes.
Confirm the spec asserts a height of at least 44.

K-022338.example: min-h-11 renders as 2.75rem, which is 44px with a 16px root font size, so a bounding box of 44 passes. h-8 renders at 32px and fails the target.
K-022338.check: The grep prints the min-h-11 class line, and Playwright prints N passed with the bounding box height at 44 or more.
traps: rem values scale with the root font size, so check the measured box instead of assuming 44px.
A dark-mode border or ring can add pixels and change the measured height.
Changing only colors does not change size, so run the size check after any padding or border edit.

steps.do: Build the production bundle so the test uses compiled CSS.
Start the preview server on port 4173 and leave it running in its own terminal.
Create the reports folder for the Lighthouse JSON output.
Run Lighthouse accessibility on the dark route and write the result as JSON.
Read the accessibility score from the JSON report.

K-022339.example: The dark route is served from dist after the build, and the report prints 1 for a score of 100. A button with gray-500 text on gray-900 lowers the score below 1 and lists color-contrast in the report.
K-022339.check: jq prints 1, which means a Lighthouse accessibility score of 100.
traps: A score of 1 does not check focus ring contrast, because Lighthouse audits only the rendered page at load time.
Lighthouse tests the built CSS, so a stale dist folder can hide your latest dark: changes.
The preview server must stay running during the Lighthouse step or the run fails.

steps.do: Create the widget folder if it does not exist.
Create the empty widget file lib/widgets/animated_text_field.dart.
In a StatefulWidget, create a FocusNode in initState and dispose it in dispose.
Wrap the TextField in an AnimatedContainer with duration Duration(milliseconds: 200), curve Curves.easeOut, and a BoxDecoration border color that depends on focusNode.hasFocus.
Set the TextField decoration to InputBorder.none so only the AnimatedContainer border shows.
Confirm the duration is exactly 200 milliseconds.
Run the analyzer on the new file.

K-022340.example: The unfocused border is Color(0xFF9E9E9E) at width 1.0 and the focused border is Color(0xFF1565C0) at width 2.0, animated over Duration(milliseconds: 200) with Curves.easeOut. rg prints the line containing Duration(milliseconds: 200).
K-022340.check: rg prints one line containing Duration(milliseconds: 200) and dart analyze prints No issues found!
traps: AnimatedContainer only animates values that change between builds, so the border must be recomputed in build. Forgetting to dispose the FocusNode leaks a listener. Setting the duration to 2000 instea…

steps.do: Add SingleTickerProviderStateMixin to the State class and declare a late AnimationController named shakeController with duration Duration(milliseconds: 400).
Build a TweenSequence that moves the offset from 0 to 8 to -8 to 0 pixels on the x axis.
Wrap the TextField in an AnimatedBuilder that applies Transform.translate with the animated dx.
Call shakeController.reset and then shakeController.forward inside the validation failure branch.
Call shakeController.dispose inside dispose before super.dispose.
Create the widget test file for the shake behavior.
Run the shake test.
Search for every AnimationController in the widgets folder to confirm each has a dispose call.

K-022341.example: On submit with empty text the controller plays for 400ms and moves dx through 0, 8, -8, and back to 0 pixels. The test pumps Duration(milliseconds: 200) and expects the Transform offset dx to be nonzero.
K-022341.check: flutter test prints All tests passed! and rg lists one AnimationController declaration plus one dispose line.
traps: Calling forward on a controller that already finished at 1.0 does nothing unless reset runs first. Skipping dispose causes a Ticker is still active error. Use SingleTickerProviderStateMixin for one c…

steps.do: Wrap the error Text in an AnimatedSwitcher with duration Duration(milliseconds: 150) and transitionBuilder that returns a FadeTransition.
Give each error Text a ValueKey built from its message so AnimatedSwitcher detects changes.
Return SizedBox.shrink when there is no error so the switcher animates to an empty child.
Format the widget file.
Analyze the widgets folder.
Create the test file for the error switcher.
Run that test file.

K-022342.example: When the error changes from null to Required the switcher fades the new Text in over 150ms, and when it becomes null the child becomes SizedBox.shrink. The test calls tester.pump(Duration(milliseconds: 150)) and expects find.byType(FadeTransition) to find one widget.
K-022342.check: dart format reports Formatted 1 file or Unchanged, flutter analyze prints No issues found!, and flutter test prints All tests passed!
traps: A Text without a ValueKey makes AnimatedSwitcher skip the fade because the widget type is unchanged. Without SizedBox.shrink the layout jumps instead of collapsing. A single pump can stop mid-fade, s…

steps.do: Add a suffixIcon to InputDecoration that is an IconButton wrapped in AnimatedScale with scale 1.0 when the text is not empty and 0.0 when it is empty.
Set the AnimatedScale duration to Duration(milliseconds: 150) with curve Curves.easeOutBack.
Wrap the scaled IconButton in IgnorePointer that is ignoring when the text is empty.
Set the IconButton constraints to BoxConstraints with minWidth 48 and minHeight 48 logical pixels.
Confirm the 150 duration and the 48 minimum size are in the file.
Analyze the widgets folder.

K-022343.example: When the text is nonempty the clear icon scales to 1.0 over 150ms, and when the field is empty it scales to 0.0 and ignores taps. rg prints the line containing Duration(milliseconds: 150) with the 150 value.
K-022343.check: rg prints at least one matching line containing 150 and dart analyze prints No issues found!
traps: A scale of 0.0 still keeps the IconButton in the tree, so it can still take taps unless IgnorePointer wraps it. A 24 pixel icon does not mean a 24 pixel tap target, so keep the 48 pixel minimum. Forg…

steps.do: Read the flag at the top of build with MediaQuery.disableAnimationsOf(context).
Set the animation duration to Duration.zero when the flag is true and Duration(milliseconds: 200) otherwise.
Search the widgets folder for every Duration to confirm none is hardcoded on the disabled path.
Create the reduced motion test file.
In the test, wrap the field in MediaQuery with data copyWith disableAnimations set to true, then pump one frame.
Run the reduced motion test file.
Run the full test suite to catch regressions.

K-022344.example: The test wraps the field in MediaQuery with disableAnimations true, pumps one frame, and expects the AnimatedContainer duration to equal Duration.zero. rg lists the computed duration line, and no hardcoded Duration(milliseconds: 200) appears on the disabled path.
K-022344.check: flutter test prints All tests passed! and rg shows the duration computed from disableAnimationsOf rather than a bare constant.
traps: Duration.zero still needs one pump, so tests that expect a settled frame must call pumpAndSettle. Reading window.accessibilityFeatures instead of MediaQuery misses the widget-level override. One hard…

steps.do: Create the goldens folder if it does not exist.
Create the golden test file.
In a testWidgets body, tap the field, pump Duration(milliseconds: 200) to settle the animation, then call expectLater with matchesGoldenFile for animated_text_field_focused.png.
Generate the golden image once from the test.
Run the golden test without the update flag to compare pixels.
List the golden folder to confirm the PNG exists.
Print the PNG size in bytes to confirm the file is not empty.

K-022345.example: The golden test taps the field, pumps 200ms, and compares against test/goldens/animated_text_field_focused.png. stat prints a byte count above zero, such as 3120.
K-022345.check: flutter test without the update flag prints All tests passed!, and stat prints a number greater than 0.
traps: Running with --update-goldens on a broken widget saves the bug into the image. Pump the full 200 milliseconds so the screenshot is not a mid-animation frame. Golden images differ across operating sys…

steps.do: Create the css folder inside onboarding.
Create the onboarding page file.
Create the stylesheet file in the css folder.
Inside head, add meta charset utf-8, a viewport meta tag with width=device-width and initial-scale=1, and a link tag with rel stylesheet and href css/onboarding.css.
Confirm the viewport meta tag exists exactly once.
Confirm the stylesheet link comes before the closing head tag by comparing line numbers. The stylesheet line number must be smaller than the </head> line number.
Run the HTML validator on the page and check for zero errors.

K-022346.example: The head element holds meta charset utf-8, the viewport meta tag, and link rel stylesheet href css/onboarding.css. The grep command prints 1.
K-022346.check: mkdir -p creates onboarding/css. grep -c viewport onboarding/index.html prints 1. grep -n -e stylesheet -e '</head>' onboarding/index.html prints a stylesheet line number lower than the </head> line number. npx --yes html-validate onboarding/index.html exits with code 0 and reports no errors.
traps: Small models leave out the viewport meta tag, so phones render the page at desktop width.
Writing max-width media queries first makes the layout harder to extend.
Do not put the stylesheet link after the body element.

steps.do: Confirm the toast file exists at the expected path.
Count hardcoded fontSize lines in the toast file; the count must be 0.
Count TextStyle constructor uses in the toast file; the count must be 0 so styles come from the theme.
Run the analyzer on the toast file and expect no issues.

K-022347.example: The toast file has 0 fontSize matches and 0 TextStyle matches, and dart analyze reports No issues found!. A Text widget with fontSize 15 would make the fontSize count 1 and fail this check.
K-022347.check: grep -c prints 0 for fontSize and for TextStyle, and dart analyze prints No issues found!.
traps: Small models add a TextStyle with a literal fontSize inside the toast and call it done. The source must be Theme.of(context).textTheme.bodyMedium, with copyWith used only for color.
grep -c exits with status 1 when the count is 0. That is the correct result, not a failure.

steps.do: Confirm the contrast test file exists.
Write a test that computes the ratio from Color.computeLuminance() of the text color and the inverseSurface background, and asserts the ratio is at least 4.5.
Run the contrast test.
Confirm the 4.5 threshold is written in the test file.

K-022348.example: The light toast uses onInverseSurface #FFFFFF on inverseSurface #323232, a ratio of about 12.8:1, which passes. The text color #7A7A7A on #323232 gives about 3.0:1, which fails the 4.5:1 floor.
K-022348.check: flutter test prints All tests passed! and grep prints a line containing 4.5.
traps: Small models compute the ratio from sRGB values directly and skip linearization. Use the luminance formula from Color.computeLuminance, which applies the gamma correction.
A test that only checks that the color is not null proves nothing. The assertion must compare the computed ratio against 4.5.

steps.do: Confirm the golden test file exists.
Run the golden test, which compares the rendered toast to the saved PNG files with matchesGoldenFile.
List the golden PNG files; expect two, one for text scale 1.0 and one for 2.0.
Regenerate goldens only after an intentional visual change, then review the new PNGs before committing.

K-022349.example: The goldens toast_default_scale.png and toast_text_scale_2.png are compared on every run. If bodyMedium changes from 14 to 15 logical pixels, the run fails with a pixel diff message.
K-022349.check: flutter test prints All tests passed! and ls prints toast_default_scale.png and toast_text_scale_2.png.
traps: Small models regenerate goldens to hide a real failure. A change that breaks the diff must be fixed in the widget, not in the PNG.
Golden output depends on the font and platform. Generate the files on the same OS that runs in CI.

steps.do: Confirm the token file exists.
Confirm AppTokens extends ThemeExtension in the token file.
Confirm the toast radius token is declared with the value 12.0.
Run the token unit test that asserts toastRadius is 12.0 and toastBodySize is 14.0.
Analyze the token file for type errors.

K-022350.example: AppTokens declares toastRadius = 12.0 and toastBodySize = 14.0 inside a ThemeExtension<AppTokens>. The test fails if a later edit changes toastRadius to 13.0.
K-022350.check: grep prints a line containing extends ThemeExtension<AppTokens>, flutter test prints All tests passed!, and dart analyze prints No issues found!.
